name: Yashwant Das
subtitle: Lead QA Engineer & Test Automation Architect • AI-Assisted Quality Engineering
heroSummary: I build the systems that decide whether software ships. For twelve years that has meant streaming platforms watched by millions, checkout flows moving real money, and Android handsets shipping to three continents. Now it also means teaching language models to write and repair tests — while deterministic checks, not the model, still decide what passes.
about:
Most of my career has gone into one question — what does "working" actually mean here? — and then building the machinery to answer it before a customer does.

That machinery looks different everywhere. At an OTT vendor it meant proving video played correctly on a Smart TV in Singapore, an Xbox in Australia and a phone in India, with DRM intact on every one. At a retail platform serving 35M+ customers it meant checkout and payments, in Spanish, across four Latin American markets. At an enterprise consultancy it meant cloud media QC for Paramount, and frameworks that ten engineers could work in without standing on each other.

Lately the interesting problem is AI. I'm skeptical of QA systems that treat model output as ground truth, so the tools I build keep the two apart: a model can generate a test, read a failure and propose a repair — but an AST-level patch, a re-run and a deterministic assertion decide whether it was right. Every call is traced. Every claim is benchmarked.

highlights: Published six open-source projects: AI-assisted Playwright tooling (structured test generation, AST-based self-healing, benchmark-driven evaluation), LLM output evaluation with Promptfoo, and reference frameworks for Selenium 4 on Java 21 and distributed load testing with Locust, Prometheus and Grafana.
Pursuing a Bachelor of Computer Applications at Manipal University Jaipur (expected 2029).

Client: Pilot Flying J. Arrived at programme start with no automation in place and left with a Playwright framework the web and mobile streams both ran on, plus an API suite shared with the team in Romania.
Grew and trained a ten-person QE team across three workstreams — most of them new to the framework, all of them shipping in it within weeks.
Moved test design into sprint planning rather than after it, so quality work stopped arriving late by default.
Upskilled in Playwright (Java) and Python test automation (pytest, Selenium); the resulting frameworks were published on GitHub in April–May 2025.
Owned automation architecture across three enterprise programmes at once — media, insurance and financial services — five to ten engineers each, one set of shared conventions between them.
For Paramount, built cloud media QC automation checking audio, video quality and encoding integrity across streaming and post-production, plus performance testing of playback at scale.
Built internal tooling for test creation, data validation and visual checks, and spent real time killing flaky tests — the quiet work that decides whether anyone trusts the suite.
Led transitions and knowledge transfer as Transition Champion, which mostly meant making myself unnecessary on the way out.
Led a team of five on Falabella's e-commerce platform — web and native apps, with checkout and payments as the part that could not be wrong.
Built cross-platform BDD automation in Cucumber and Appium, then wired it into the release pipeline so regression stopped being a manual event.
Ran QA across Chile, Peru, Colombia and Argentina, Spanish-language localisation included. Four markets, one suite.
Four streaming clients — Optus Sport, ALTBalaji, Mediacorp and FOX — across web, mobile, Smart TVs, Apple TV, Xbox and Fire TV. Same content, very different players, all expected to just work.
Took apps through Microsoft Xbox and Amazon Fire TV store certification, where the bar is someone else's checklist and there is no arguing with it.
Used Conviva telemetry and log analysis to turn "the video looks bad" into something specific enough to fix.
Validated geo-restrictions, regional catalogues and streaming protocols for launches in Australia, India, Singapore and the US.
Trained at Gionee's Shenzhen headquarters, then built and ran the digital image and audio quality lab in India — where camera, display and audio claims either held up or didn't.
Wrote Android instrumented automation for media and image quality, alongside performance and stability runs.
Automated Android testing across phones, tablets and feature phones with Appium and UI Automator.
Defined the test approach for new device launches — OS compatibility and third-party app integration, on hardware that changed every few months.
Automated post-launch testing for the Nokia Lumia series.
Android platform testing with the Compatibility Test Suite, and automation for Samsung devices and apps.
Validated DRM compliance for Samsung Media Service and Media Hub (AT&T) — the first time streaming rights were my problem, and not the last.
Where it started: Xbox, PlayStation 3 and PSP titles — Demon's Souls, Toy Story, Enslaved: Odyssey to the West — playing the same level until it broke.

projects.title: Testing LLM Automation Engine
projects.description: An LLM + vision AI automation framework for Playwright that addresses three core challenges: generating TypeScript tests from DOM context, generating tests from screenshots using multimodal vision models, and automatically healing broken specs. The self-healer runs an auditable Monitor → Investigate → Reason → Act → Report pipeline, combining deterministic heuristics for fast error classification with LLM reasoning. Every repair emits a structured HealingDecision artifact with confidence scoring, diagnostic evidence, code patches, and verification results.

projects.title: Smart Playwright Protocol
projects.description: SPP is a protocol-driven workflow for AI-assisted Playwright automation — defining an auditable contract for how AI agents and engineers collaborate on test tasks. It enforces a strict 6-phase engineering lifecycle (Select → Understand → Explore → Plan → Implement → Verify) using Markdown task contracts, deterministic verification gates, and Page Object best practices. Features a dedicated CLI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server integration to manage task state and coordinate autonomous agents under explicit engineering control.

projects.title: Offline AI Toolkit for Apple Silicon
projects.description: Offline-first local AI toolkit built on MLX. Audio transcription with MLX Whisper, meeting summaries through Ollama, and vision analysis with Moondream and LLaMA 3.2 — no API keys, nothing leaves the machine.

projects.title: Distributed Load Testing Stack
projects.description: Locust master/worker cluster with Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards and custom alerting, orchestrated with Docker Compose. Multi-scenario load profiles and real observability rather than a single summary number.

projects.title: LLM Evaluation with Promptfoo
projects.description: Translation-quality evaluation for local models, run entirely offline through Ollama and LM Studio. Treats model output as something to be measured against assertions, not trusted.

projects.title: Selenium 4 Reference Framework (Java 21)
projects.description: Reference-grade Selenium 4 and TestNG framework on Java 21: Page Object Model, parallel execution, Allure reporting, REST Assured for API coverage, and Checkstyle quality gates.

projects.title: Python Selenium Framework
projects.description: pytest and Selenium WebDriver framework with Page Object Model, parallel execution, Allure reports and multi-environment configuration.
